Finding intent in the conversation

An LLM-powered system that finds buying and selling signals in communication streams, then alerts the agent when a prospect needs help.

The workflow, at a glance

01Communication streams02Intent extraction03Agent alert

A simplified view of the workflow.

The problem

A prospect’s next move can be buried in an ordinary reply. Real estate teams need a way to notice those signals across newsletters, drip campaigns, and ongoing conversations.

What I built

The system ingests communication streams and uses LLM reasoning to extract explicit and implicit buying or selling intent. It sends real-time alerts to agents when a prospect needs assistance.

This is the current main product at Clarity Works. It brings together the work I enjoy most: understanding the operational problem and translating it into a working AI pipeline.

Where it stands

The product is live in pilot testing. I’m keeping that distinction clear: a deployed pilot is an important step, and its broader business impact still needs to be measured.

The design question

How do you distinguish a useful signal from a plausible interpretation? For an intent system, that question matters as much as the extraction itself. It is the part of the work I want to make visible as the pilot develops.
